catholic-encyclopedia-1913-berthold-schw:
Berthold Schwarz, a German friar reputed inventor of gunpowder and firearms, is the subject of this 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry. Opinion differs sharply about the man behind the name and his share in the discovery. He was a Franciscan, said to have been born at Freiburg during the early thirteenth century.

Berthold was his religious name, with Schwarz, or black, added for his habit's colour or for supposed dealings in the black art. In alchemical study he is said to have found gunpowder's explosive force and applied it to guns. A monument at Freiburg honours the claim, which the entry treats as tradition rather than proof.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-goerz:
Goerz, in Italian Gorizia and Slovene Gorica, is the capital of the Austrian crown-land of Görz and Gradiska. Its population in 1900 was 25,432, almost exclusively Catholic, 68 per cent Italians, 20 per cent Slovenes, and 11.6 per cent Germans. A Catholic Encyclopedia article traces a borderland passed from counts to emperors.

An archbishop has sat at Görz since 1751, as metropolitan of the ecclesiastical province of Illyria. The town was recognized as such only in 1307, though the counts took their title from its castle much earlier. At the death of the last count, Leonhard, in 1500 without issue, the territory fell to Emperor Maximilian I. Apart from French occupation from 1809 to 1815, it has stayed with the house of Austria.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-thomas-of-jor: Jorz was the cardinal of the Dominicans. This entry traces his 1200s, his England, and his Rome. The theologian of the Oxford schools: his brief cardinalate crowned Rome in the 1300s of the Boniface in the truly very old curia.
